Reuters reported Prime Minister Takaichi strongly hoping the Bank of Japan achieves wage-driven inflation, while a draft stimulus package pointed toward a bold spending increase. Wage-led inflation implies household purchasing power and consumption improving together; a weaker yen that mainly raises import costs is a less favorable route. Fiscal announcements become more valuable when implementation and funding are credible, and less valuable when bond and currency markets demand a larger risk premium. [[n3623]] [[n3643]]

Bloomberg reported Takaichi looking toward a stimulus package to advance the growth plan, while CNBC described declining real wages as inflation reduced purchasing power. Wage growth that exceeds household costs would support consumption more durably than a weaker currency that mainly increases import bills. Favor businesses with identifiable earnings drivers and avoid paying for proposed support as if every funding and execution decision were already settled. [[n3573]] [[n3529]]
